A1.justification: Both readable 11-page PDFs describe the same research work, substantially revised and renamed in v2. Their main text, equations, figures and tables support comparison. However, neither contains appendices: v1 references supplementary implementation details and analyses, while v2 references unavailable ScaleAttention pseudocode, limiting comparison of that material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, few-shot learning, segmentation and detection results in Tables 1–5, plus ablations and reconstruction visualizations.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification, segmentation and detection results, including multiple model variants, alongside component and modality ablations in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: v1 reconstructs masked point clouds and multi-view depth images through a joint decoder. v2 retains feature projection but introduces fusion encoding, separate 2D/3D decoders with multi-scale multi-head attention, and two-stage training: an unmasked reconstruction teacher supervises a masked student through token-level and instance-level feature losses. These substantially change the architecture and learning procedure.

E1.justification: The five datasets and the principal classification, segmentation and detection tasks remain. However, v1's explicit ModelNet40 few-shot learning evaluation, covering 5/10-way and 10/20-shot settings, is absent from the supplied v2, narrowing coverage of learning with limited labels.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Point-GPT, ACT, I2P-MAE and ReCon to classification comparisons while removing Point-BERT and older supervised comparators. Segmentation adds ACT, I2P-MAE and ReCon but removes PointNet++ and DGCNN. Detection removes Hou et al. and 4DContrast. These substantially revise comparator membership within the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: v2 evaluates additional Point-M2AE configurations and integrations with I2P-MAE and ReCon, and adds ModelNet40 testing without voting alongside voting. Its new controlled ablations use ScanObjectNN PB-T50-RS, whereas v1's ablations use OBJ-BG and OBJ-ONLY. Missing training-budget disclosures do not establish that those settings changed.

E4.justification: v1 tests pose-pool size, reconstructed-view count and joint-decoder/modality-loss combinations, and shows reconstruction examples. Those analyses are absent from the supplied v2. Instead, v2 Tables 4–5 test combinations of token prediction, instance prediction and MSMH attention, and compare input/output modalities, substantially changing the questions investigated.

E5.justification: v1 Table 3 and Section 4.2 report few-shot means and standard deviations over ten independent experiments. That experiment and its uncertainty reporting disappear in v2. The retained benchmark comparisons continue to report point estimates; neither version supplies comparable uncertainty reporting for those results.

E6.justification: For the revised Point-MAE-based method, ScanObjectNN scores change from 92.94/92.08/87.23 to 93.32/92.69/88.93; voted ModelNet40 accuracy remains 94.1. Segmentation instance mIoU changes from 86.57 to 86.79, and detection AP25/AP50 from 64.0/42.9 to 63.9/43.3. v2 also adds substantial variant and ablation results while omitting few-shot results. Changed methods and incomplete training documentation limit interpretation as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 introduces formal definitions of grouped multi-scale attention in Equations 5–6 and latent token, intra-modality and inter-modality prediction objectives in Equations 7–10. These substantially extend the mathematical formulation beyond v1's raw point/depth reconstruction objective. Neither version provides theorems or proofs; the change concerns mathematical definitions of the method.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from pose-aware multi-view masked reconstruction to a framework claiming novel MSMH attention and two-stage representation alignment. v2 additionally emphasizes the detrimental reliance on visible 2D inputs and complementarity with foundation-model features. The earlier explicit few-shot performance claim is dropped.

C2.justification: v2 newly argues that visible 2D inputs leak viewpoint information and hinder geometric learning, and interprets integrations with I2P-MAE/ReCon as evidence that geometric and semantic features are complementary. It adds explanations for local/global attention and feature distillation, while omitting v1's explanations of excessive-view redundancy and decoder-sequence limitations.

D1.justification: v1 specifies AdamW, cosine decay, 300 epochs, batch size 128, learning rate 0.0002, weight decay 0.05, masking ratio 0.75, 1,024 input points and three reconstructed views. v2 omits these explicit settings and the abstract's future code-release pointer. It adds image token size 16, 196 tokens per view and encoder partitioning details, but its referenced pseudocode appendix is absent.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around geometric learning complementary to foundation-model semantic distillation, particularly I2P-MAE and ReCon. It removes the broad 3D self-supervised learning subsection, revises the multimodal discussion around two-stage alignment, and adds works including Point-GPT, MultiMAE and contrastive audio-visual MAE. This exceeds bibliographic updating.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, the method is renamed from Multiview-MAE to Multiview-ML, and the title and author list change. The method section replaces its Point-MAE tutorial with reorganized component descriptions; related work and experiments are restructured, and the separate visualization section disappears.

P2.justification: The overview and joint-decoder graphics are substantially redrawn for the teacher/fusion architecture. v2 adds a projection illustration and teacher–student diagram while removing v1's introductory comparison graphic and reconstruction examples. Separate classification tables become a combined table with foundation-model and voting columns, and the ablation displays are replaced.

improvement.justification: v2's component and input-modality controls better test its proposed mechanisms, while integrations with I2P-MAE and ReCon strengthen evidence of applicability across methods. However, its substantially more complex training procedure loses v1's explicit optimization settings and code-release pointer, and the promised implementation appendix is absent. The stronger empirical support and weaker reproducibility leave the net quality direction uncertain.
